claim: For the Hide–Skeldon–Acheson system \(\dot x=x(y-1)-\beta z,\ \dot y=\alpha(1-x^2)-ky,\ \dot z=x-bz\) with \(\alpha,\beta,b,k>0\), the equilibrium \(E=(0,\alpha/k,0)\) is globally asymptotically stable for every \(0<\alpha\le k\). The quadratic function \(V=\alpha x^2+(y-\alpha/k)^2+\alpha\beta z^2\) obeys the exact identity \(\dot V=-2\alpha(k-\alpha)x^2/k-2k(y-\alpha/k)^2-2\alpha\beta b z^2\). For \(0<\alpha<k\) this is negative definite away from \(E\); for \(\alpha=k\), the largest invariant subset of \(\{\dot V=0\}=\{y=1,z=0\}\) is \(E\), because invariance of \(z=0\) forces \(x=0\). Hence LaSalle's invariance principle gives global attraction also at the boundary. This strictly strengthens the 2022 global-stability criterion, which additionally requires \(k(\alpha\beta-1)^2+4\alpha b(\alpha-k)<0\) and \(k>\alpha\).
integrity: The proof is self-contained from the printed vector field; the key derivative identity was independently re-expanded, and the comparison to the 2022 theorem uses its full-text statement.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is a sufficient global-stability result for positive parameters on \(0<\alpha\le k\); it does not claim necessity or classify dynamics for \(\alpha>k\). The 1996 model paper was not available for whole-document comparison, leaving a stated residual literature risk.
title: Global stability on the full \(\alpha\le k\) half-space of the Hide–Skeldon–Acheson dynamo
